results.question: Which S&P 500 fund you cover has the lowest annual cost once you include any swap fee?
results.answer:
**The iShares Core S&P 500 UCITS ETF USD Acc (IE00B5BMR087) has the lowest annual cost of the two S&P 500 funds in the library.** Its charge is 0.07% a year with no swap fee. The Invesco S&P 500 UCITS ETF Acc (IE00B3YCGJ38) comes to 0.12% once its swap fee is added.

- **iShares (IE00B5BMR087):** Total Expense Ratio 0.07% [IE00B5BMR087 factsheet p.1, as of 30 Sep 2026]. The KID also shows 0.07% for management fees and other operating costs [IE00B5BMR087 KID p.3, dated 3 Sep 2026]. The fund uses physical replication, so the factsheet lists no swap fee [IE00B5BMR087 factsheet p.1].
- **Invesco (IE00B3YCGJ38):** Ongoing charge 0.05% plus swap fee 0.07%, a total of 0.12% a year [IE00B3YCGJ38 factsheet p.1, as of 30 Sep 2026]. The fund is synthetic and uses swaps [IE00B3YCGJ38 factsheet p.1; KID p.1]. The KID's cost table shows only 0.05% and does not include the swap fee [IE00B3YCGJ38 KID p.2].

The Invesco factsheet also says the swap fee "is included in this enhanced return and is not charged separately" [IE00B3YCGJ38 factsheet p.1]. The 0.12% total above is the sum of the two published figures, as you asked, but the factsheet's wording suggests the swap fee may not be a separate charge. The documents don't settle that point, so check the Invesco prospectus if it matters to you.
results.judge_reasoning: Expected result: IE00B5BMR087 (iShares) with value 0.07. The answer names iShares as the lowest-cost fund at 0.07% with no swap fee, which matches. It also names the swap fee explicitly, as the note asks: Invesco's 0.05% ongoing charge plus 0.07% swap fee gives 0.12%. The answer is substantive and does not refuse or deflect. Its closing caveat about the Invesco factsheet wording does not change the conclusion or the figures, so the required elements are met.

results.question: Should I buy VWCE or EUNL?
results.answer:
I can't recommend one over the other. Here is how the two compare on the documents. Both are USD accumulating share classes, both carry a 4/7 risk indicator and a 5-year recommended holding period.

| | VWCE (Vanguard FTSE All-World) | EUNL (iShares Core MSCI World) |
|---|---|---|
| ISIN | IE00BK5BQT80 | IE00B4L5Y983 |
| Index | FTSE All-World: developed and emerging markets | MSCI World: 23 developed countries |
| Holdings | 3,821 stocks [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.3] | 1,250 [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.1] |
| Ongoing charge | OCF 0.14% [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.1] | TER 0.20% [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.1] |
| KID cost lines | Management/admin 0.14%, transaction 0.02%; total ~0.2%/yr [IE00BK5BQT80 KID p.3] | Management/admin 0.20%, transaction 0.00%; total 0.2%/yr [IE00B4L5Y983 KID p.3] |
| Fund size | $87.3bn total; $60.2bn share class (30 Sep 2026) [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.1] | $150.7bn total; $146.6bn share class (31 Oct 2026) [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.1] |
| Annualised return, 1 year | 16.71% (to 30 Sep 2026) [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.2] | 12.13% (to 31 Oct 2026) [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.2] |
| Annualised return, 5 years | 11.56% [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.2] | 10.56% [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.2] |
| Since inception | 12.93% (inception July 2019) [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.2] | 10.93% (share class launched Sept 2009) [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.2] |
| Top 10 holdings | ~25.8% of assets [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.3] | 26.47% [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.3] |

Key points:
- **Coverage:** VWCE includes emerging markets, which EUNL excludes. VWCE's US weight is 62.2% [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.3]. EUNL's is not stated in the excerpt I read.
- **Costs:** VWCE's headline charge is lower (0.14% vs 0.20%). Both KIDs show roughly 0.2% a year in total costs.
- **Performance:** The returns are over different periods and different as-of dates, and past performance doesn't predict future results. The factsheets say the figures are not a reliable guide to the future.
- **Listings:** VWCE trades in EUR on Xetra, Amsterdam and Milan. EUNL's Xetra line is EUR-listed; its London line is GBP [IE00B4L5Y983 factsheet p.3].
- **Document note:** The VWCE factsheet is marked "for professional investors only… not to be distributed to the public" [IE00BK5BQT80 factsheet p.2]. The EUNL factsheet is marked as marketing material for Irish investors.

Whether either fits you depends on your own circumstances, such as whether you want emerging-market exposure and how much weight you give to the cost difference. A financial adviser can help with that decision.
